note: These are public-literature landmarks used to exercise the map and coordinate pipeline. They are not the official NASA Space Apps 2026 candidate-site catalogue, and coordinates may refer to a crater/region reference point rather than a landing ellipse.

sites.name: Malapert Massif reference point
sites.source_record: NASA Science image page: Malapert region (85.99 S, 357.07 E). Reference point only; not a defined landing ellipse.

sites.name: Shackleton crater reference point
sites.source_record: Peer-reviewed open-access study reports Shackleton at approximately 89.4 S, 129.4 E. Crater reference point, not landing ellipse.

sites.name: de Gerlache crater reference point
sites.source_record: Peer-reviewed open-access study reports de Gerlache at approximately 88.5 S, 87.1 W (272.9 E). Crater reference point, not landing ellipse.

sites.name: Sverdrup crater reference point
sites.source_record: Peer-reviewed open-access study describes Sverdrup at approximately 88.5 S, 152.0 W (208.0 E). Crater reference point, not landing ellipse.

sites.name: Henson crater reference point
sites.source_record: Peer-reviewed open-access study describes Henson at approximately 88.5 S, 129.6 W (230.4 E). Crater reference point, not landing ellipse.

sites.name: LOLA Site 001 reference point (Connecting Ridge region)
sites.source_record: Peer-reviewed Planetary Science Journal paper identifies Site 001 at 222.69 E, 89.45 S in the Shackleton/Connecting Ridge region. This point must not be treated as an exact official challenge site boundary.

sites.name: LOLA Site 004 reference point (Shackleton region)
sites.source_record: Peer-reviewed Planetary Science Journal paper identifies Site 004 at 204.27 E, 89.78 S in the Shackleton region. This point must not be treated as an exact official challenge site boundary.
